([[Torrelodones]], [[Spain]]) | college = *[[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]] (2020–2023) *[[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]] (2023–present) | highlights = * [[Atlantic 10 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic 10 Player of the Year]] (2025) * 2× First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] (2024, 2025) }} '''Maksym "Max" Shulga''' (born June 25, 2002) is a Ukrainian [[college basketball]] player for the [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU Rams]]. He previously played for the [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State Aggies]]. ==Early life and education== Shulga was born and grew up in [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]].{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/basketball/vcu/men/article_acc65902-f653-11ef-9c90-9b8357ce80ee.html|title=VCU fans plan 'moment for Max,' will fly Ukrainian flags at Shulga's last home game|first=Zach|last=Joachim|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=March 3, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He moved to Spain at age 11 to study and play basketball in Colegio Leones in León At age 14 he moved to Madrid to attend the Basketball School of Excellence in [[Torrelodones]].{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/sean-bairstow-max-shulga-vcu-basketball-ryan-odom-utah-state-rams/article_58b784a8-2fc1-11ee-8b3d-fb66a118a41f.html|title=VCU basketball transfers Bairstow, Shulga share close bond|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=August 3, 2023|access-date=March 5, 2025}} Shulga committed to play college basketball in the United States at [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/5/20/21265294/utah-state-university-aggies-mens-basketball-commit-ukrainian-national-max-shulga/|title=Utah State men's basketball adds another commit in Ukrainian national Max Shulga|first=Trent|last=Wood|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=May 20, 2020|access-date=March 3, 2025}} ==College career== Shulga began his college career at [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-state-sports/2022/03/01/he-prepares-his-next-game/|title=Utah State’s Max Shulga’s thoughts are with his family in Ukraine as he prepares for Aggies’ next game|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=March 1, 2022|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He was named honorable mention All-[[Mountain West Conference]] as a junior after averaging 11.9 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game. After the season and the departure of Aggies' head coach [[Ryan Odom]], he entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-state-sports/2023/04/03/2-utah-state-basketball-starters/|title=2 Utah State basketball starters enter transfer portal|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=March 1, 2025}} Shulga transferred to [[VCU Rams men's basketball|VCU]], following Odom.{{cite web|url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/vcu-hoops-lands-utah-state-transfers-sean-bairstow-max-shulga/article_23359244-e240-11ed-9bbd-b3d1894db7a9.html|title=VCU basketball lands Utah State transfers Shulga, Bairstow|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|date=April 23, 2023|access-date=March 5, 2025}} He was named first-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] in his first season with the Rams after averaging 14.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/villanova-basketball-max-shulga-commit-transfer-portal-20240503.html|title=VCU transfer Max Shulga gives Villanova playmaking and shooting as its roster continues to take shape|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=May 3, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2025}} Shulga re-entered the transfer portal at the end of the season and initially committed to transfer to [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], but ultimately decommitted and returned to VCU.{{cite web|url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/villanova/max-shulga-decomits-villanova-vcu-20240522.html|title=Max Shulga withdraws his commitment to Villanova and plans to return to VCU|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=May 22, 2024|access-date=March 3, 2025}} In his final year at VCU, Shulga averaged a career-high 15.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game, {{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/max-shulga-1.html|title=Max Shulga|date=March 21, 2025|access-date=May 21, 2025|publisher=sports-reference.com}} while leading the Rams to win both the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] regular-season and [[Atlantic 10 Men's Basketball Tournament]] championships. They won 18 of their final 20 games en route to a No. 11 seed in the NCAA tournament, where they lost to No. 6 seed [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in the first round. {{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44343773/vcu-ryan-odom-emerges-top-virginia-candidate|title=VCU's Ryan Odom hired as Virginia men's basketball coach|date=March 21, 2025|accessdate=March 22, 2025|first1=Pete|last1=Thamel|first2=Jeff|last2=Borzello|publisher=espn.com}} Shulga is considered a potential NBA prospect and was one of 75 players invited to the 2025 [[NBA draft combine|NBA Draft Combine]] in May of 2025. {{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-draft-combine-list-of-invites|title=NBA announces 75 players invited to participate at 2025 NBA
